title: Shard churn & KV-prefetch streaming load harness
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Create a scalable load harness for SSE/WebSocket streaming chat that emulates realistic session churn across sharded serving pools and exercises prefix/KV cache prefetch behavior. The harness will produce tokens/sec profiles, per-session p95 latency telemetry, and automatic regression detection alerts when throughput or p95 degrades beyond configured gates. It must be configurable to run against hosted, dedicated, and private endpoints with tenancy and routing policy variations.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can spawn 50k concurrent streaming sessions (mix of SSE and WS) with configurable churn patterns
Per-session and aggregated metrics emitted to the telemetry pipeline: tokens/sec, token latency, p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and end-to-end, and KV cache hit/miss ratios
Built-in regression detection: daily baseline comparison with automated alert when p95 increases by >15% or tokens/sec drops by >12%
KV-prefetch simulation: ability to mark a subset of sessions as 'prefetch-enabled' and measure downstream cache warmup benefit
Chaos injection knobs: intermittent kernel latency, simulated eviction storms, and occasional partial shard failures with automatic retry verification
Runbook and dashboard: a preconfigured dashboard link and a runbook that documents how to interpret failures and open PR templates for performance fixes
success_metrics: Sustained 40k tokens/sec end-to-end in baseline scenario on the benchmark cluster
Stable p95 end-to-end < 350ms in 95% of runs for baseline configuration
Regression detector false positive rate < 5% over one month of smoke runs
KV-prefetch experiments show >8% token cost savings for long-lived sessions (median session length > 20 tokens)
implementation_notes: We will implement the harness in Go to reuse existing client codepaths and integrate with the in-house load-orchestration service. Sessions are lightweight stateful workers that maintain a KV-aware prefix cache in the client which can be toggled between warm/cold starts. The harness must support multiplexing many virtual sessions per physical worker, and use a pluggable traffic profile grammar to produce conversational patterns. Telemetry will be emitted to the metric pipeline via OTLP and use existing labels (model, shard_id, route, tenant, protocol). Regression detection will be implemented as a daily job that compares the previous successful baseline window to the latest window and posts findings to the perf-alert Slack channel and the perf-dashboard. Exported artifacts must include raw event logs for post-mortem replay. Keep external dependencies minimal and avoid adding new long-lived infra services.
tradeoffs_decisions: Language choice: Go for low-latency networking and reuse of existing harness components over Rust to reduce ramp time
KV-prefetch fidelity: Simulate prefix cache behavior within the client instead of instrumenting server-side KV internals to avoid coupling to runtime internals
Multiplexing density: Favor moderate multiplexing (up to 100 virtual sessions per worker) to balance resource isolation and scaling complexity
Regression detection thresholding: Use conservative thresholds initially (15% p95, 12% throughput) to limit noise; allow teams to opt into stricter gates for release-critical models
comments: 2026-01-14 Aisha Verma: Created initial ticket and scoped acceptance criteria after sync with Runtime PM. Identified need to compare hosted vs dedicated under identical workload.

2026-01-28 Luca Martinez: Spike complete — prototype clients can open 5k concurrent SSE connections from a single 32-vCPU machine using multiplexed goroutines. Found gap in our OTLP labels for shard_id; opened PR to add label schema. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1302

2026-02-09 Infrastructure: Deployed benchmark cluster with two dedicated node pools (benchmark and target). Observed kernel-level NIC interrupts causing tail latency on high-concurrency runs — filed ENG-968001 to track kernel tunables investigation.

2026-02-22 Performance: Added KV-prefetch toggle and saw early evidence of 6% token reduction for long-lived simulated sessions in canary runs. Need larger sample size to validate across model families.

2026-02-28 Design review (PM/Eng): Agreed to implement regression detector as independent daily job that writes findings to perf-alerts and SLO dashboard rather than pushing immediate pager notifications. Action: add opt-in for high-severity models.

2026-03-03 QA: Ran 10 repeat runs of baseline profile; one run had p95 spike at 2x baseline coincident with eviction storms. Captured raw logs for replay and attached to the incident note in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadbench/issues/87
2026-03-10 Security: Confirmed no secrets are stored in harness; telemetry uses short-lived certs. Security review required: false

2026-03-12 Luca Martinez: Implemented chaos injection knobs and regression job; currently integrating dashboard panels and adding automated nightly smoke runs. Next: finalize runbook and schedule demo with runtime team 2026-03-18.
